key_insight: VideoNet provides a large-scale, domain-focused video dataset and benchmarks that re-center action recognition as a core challenge for modern vision-language and video models, exposing current models' weaknesses on temporal and domain-specific actions.
problem_solved: Existing VLM evaluations have deprioritized action recognition due to lack of diverse, challenging video datasets; VideoNet fills this gap by offering a standardized resource for domain-specific action understanding and benchmarking.
method: Curate and annotate a large-scale collection of videos emphasizing domain-specific, fine-grained actions with temporal segmentation and contextual metadata.
Design benchmark tasks and standardized splits that stress temporal reasoning, cross-domain generalization, and fine-grained action classification.
Evaluate state-of-the-art VLMs and specialized video models on these benchmarks to quantify gaps and provide baseline results and metrics.
impact: VideoNet gives researchers and practitioners a practical benchmark to develop and test models that truly understand temporal dynamics and domain-specific actions, accelerating progress on real-world video understanding tasks such as surveillance, sports analytics, and procedural video reasoning.
visual_elements: Dataset composition infographic (pie/bar charts) showing domains, action categories, and dataset scale
Annotated sample timeline: key video frames with temporal segments and fine-grained action labels
Benchmark performance chart comparing VLMs and specialist video models to highlight performance gaps
Taxonomy/flow diagram of domain-specific action categories and task types (classification, localization, temporal reasoning)
paper_title: VideoNet: A Large-Scale Dataset for Domain-Specific Action Recognition
paper_authors: Tanush Yadav, Mohammadreza Salehi, Jae Sung Park, Vivek Ramanujan, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
